content:
# 1 Maccabees Chapter 12 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17 | **Verses:** 53 | **Disagreements:** 32

---

## Summary
The "Spartans-as-brothers" letter (vv.6-23) generates significant disagreements around diplomatic register and the rendering of the ancient Spartan letter's claims. Trypho's treachery (vv.42-48) also shows divergent dramatic framing.

---

## Disagreements

**v.1** — "the time was favorable for him" (EMET) vs. "the time was right for him" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "the political moment was right" (PNEUMA)

**v.3** — "senate" (EMET) vs. "senate chamber" (LOGOS) vs. "Senate" (PNEUMA capitalized) — minor register difference.

**v.5** — "copy of the letters" (EMET) vs. "copy of the letter" (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA) — Greek: ἀντίγραφον τῶν ἐπιστολῶν; possibly a single letter addressed as plural. LOGOS/SOPHIA treat as singular.

**v.7** — "formerly letters were sent to Onias" (EMET) vs. "a letter was sent to Onias" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "a letter was sent to our high priest Onias" (PNEUMA adds "our")

**v.9** — "holy books" (EMET) vs. "holy scriptures" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "holy scriptures" (PNEUMA) — SOPHIA ruling: "holy scriptures."

**v.9** — "for our encouragement" — all agree; but the dismissal of the alliance ("we do not need these things") is softened differently: PNEUMA adds "actually" for rhetorical irony.

**v.10** — "lest we become estranged from you" (EMET/SOPHIA) vs. "lest we become strangers to you" (LOGOS) vs. "we do not wish to become strangers" (PNEUMA)

**v.11** — "make mention of you before the sacrifices and in the prayers" (EMET) vs. "remember you at the sacrifices we offer and in our prayers" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "in our sacrifices and in our prayers" (PNEUMA)

**v.12** — "we rejoice in your glory" (EMET/SOPHIA) vs. "we rejoice in your honor and renown" (LOGOS) vs. "we are glad to hear of your fame and prosperity" (PNEUMA)

**v.20** — "Arius king of the Spartans" — all agree; the letter is quoted verbatim across all translations.

**v.21** — "it has been found in a writing" (EMET) vs. "it has been discovered in a writing" (LOGOS) vs. "a document has come to light" (PNEUMA) vs. "it has been found in writing" (SOPHIA omits article)

**v.21** — "of the family of Abraham" — all agree; key claim of kinship.

**v.23** — "your cattle and your goods are ours, and ours are yours" — all preserve; a formulaic expression of alliance.

**v.25** — "gave them no opportunity to set foot in his territory" (EMET/SOPHIA) vs. "giving them no chance to enter his territory" (LOGOS) vs. "cutting them off before they could set foot on his territory" (PNEUMA)

**v.26** — "by night" (EMET) vs. "a night attack" (LOGOS) vs. "planned a night attack" (PNEUMA)

**v.28** — "were afraid and were troubled in their hearts" (EMET) vs. "they took fright, their hearts quailed" (LOGOS) vs. "they panicked" (PNEUMA) vs. "they were afraid, their hearts failed them" (SOPHIA)

**v.31** — "the Arabs who are called Zabadeans" (EMET) vs. "the Nabateans known as Zabadeans" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "the Nabatean tribe called the Zabadeans" (PNEUMA) — LOGOS/SOPHIA identify them as Nabateans per historical context.

**v.33** — "and the nearby fortresses" (EMET) vs. "the neighboring fortresses" (LOGOS/SOPHIA)

**v.36** — "to separate it from the city and make it isolated, so that they might not buy and sell" (EMET) vs. "to isolate the citadel from the city and cut off its supply lines" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "cutting off the citadel, isolating it so its garrison could no longer buy and sell in the city" (PNEUMA most explicit)

**v.37** — "Chaphenatha" — all preserve the proper name.

**v.38** — "the lowland" (EMET) vs. "the Shephelah" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "the Shephelah" (PNEUMA) — SOPHIA prefers the geographic name; EMET translates it.

**v.39** — "sought to become king over Asia" (EMET) vs. "was plotting to seize the kingship of Asia" (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA)

**v.40** — "to seize and kill him" (EMET/LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "Jonathan out of the way — dead or captured" (PNEUMA reverses the order for rhetorical effect)

**v.42** — "he feared to stretch out his hand against him" (EMET) vs. "he was afraid to raise a hand against him" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "he froze" and "didn't dare move against Jonathan" (PNEUMA)

**v.43** — "commanded his armies to be obedient to him as to himself" (EMET) vs. "ordered his troops to obey Jonathan as they would obey himself" (LOGOS/SOPHIA)

**v.44** — "Why have you wearied all this people" (EMET/SOPHIA) vs. "Why have you put all this people to such trouble" (LOGOS) vs. "Why wear out all these men" (PNEUMA)

**v.45** — "the remaining troops and all the officials" (EMET/LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "the troops, the officials, all of it" (PNEUMA condenses)

**v.47** — "left two thousand in Galilee" — all agree.

**v.48** — "shut the gates and seized him" — all agree; PNEUMA dramatizes: "slammed them shut."
- "all those who had come with him they killed with the sword" (EMET) vs. "all who had entered with him they put to the sword" (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA)

**v.50** — "went in close formation, ready for war" (EMET) vs. "marched in close order, ready for battle" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "locked shields, prepared to sell their lives dearly" (PNEUMA dramatizes significantly)

**v.52** — "were greatly afraid" (EMET/SOPHIA) vs. "were in great fear" (LOGOS) vs. "they were afraid — deeply afraid" (PNEUMA)

**v.53** — "wipe out their memory from among men" (EMET) vs. "wipe out their name from among men" (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA) — "memory" vs. "name": Greek μνημόσυνον can mean either; "name" preferred.
